problem.text: Routing previously computed softmax over every expert, selected top-k probabilities, then renormalized the selected weights.

reasoning.text: For finite logits in exact arithmetic, softmax preserves ordering and its full-expert denominator cancels during selected-weight renormalization. Selecting logits first therefore permits a single softmax over only the selected experts.

impact.text: The change removes explicit selected-weight summation and division, and reduces softmax width from the expert count to the selected count during ordinary routing. Expert evaluation and output accumulation remain unchanged.

source_notes.text: The introducing entry 6fc153d7 describes routed expert execution, single-token EXL3 fusion, and all-expert calibration; it also records the conditional fused-buffer cardinality mismatch.

PR #26, “Superior 3INST parameters,” discusses decoder multipliers; issue #33, “Error converting model,” reports file-opening failure; issue #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” reports Cholesky failure. Their inferred relevance is only shared conversion-file context, not evidence motivating this routing optimization.

limitations: No GPU execution or latency measurement was performed. The scalar check uses Python double precision, not the router's FP16 tensor arithmetic.
Exact-arithmetic equivalence does not establish bitwise equality, identical tie handling after rounding, or behavior for nonfinite logits.

claims.text: BlockSparseMLP.forward now passes router_logits directly to torch.topk and applies torch.softmax to its returned values along the expert dimension. The two edits work together: removing the full softmax without changing normalization would incorrectly normalize raw logits by their sum.

The selected count remains num_experts_per_tok, or num_experts when activate_all_experts is true. Ordinary execution multiplies expert outputs by routing_weights before index_add_; fused execution supplies those weights to the down-projection multi-GEMM and sums its expert outputs. Neither consumer changes.

A standard-library scalar transcription compared both normalization formulas on 900 finite-logit cases with 2, 8 and 64 experts and several selected counts. Maximum absolute weight difference was 2.220446049250313e-16; this checks the algebra numerically, not repository or CUDA execution.
The inherited all-expert fused-path mismatch is carried over: the diff changes normalization but neither the fused-path guard nor buffers sized by num_experts_per_tok.

findings.description: All-expert routing still conflicts with fixed selected-expert fused buffers.
findings.trigger: One flattened token, fully EXL3 expert projections, activate_all_experts=True, and num_experts != num_experts_per_tok.
findings.expected_behavior: Evaluate all experts or use the ordinary path supporting that cardinality.
findings.actual_behavior: The first fused multi-GEMM receives num_experts indices but an output with num_experts_per_tok expert slots, violating its shape check. Inspected direct MLP callers in TransformerBlock and ParallelDecoderBlock forward params unchanged. Conversion supplies the flag during unquantized calibration; that does not establish that normal conversion reaches this fully quantized trigger.

verification.description: Compared unchanged fused allocations and routing cardinality against the native index/output shape check, then inspected decoder forwarding and calibration flag construction.
verification.limits: Conditional source-level observation; no end-to-end or GPU reproduction.

annotation.summary: Moves expert selection before softmax, eliminating redundant normalization while preserving exact-arithmetic routing weights; GPU speed and FP16 equivalence remain unmeasured.
